title: Electroporation Transformation of FITC-Dextran into Oxyrrhis Marina
author: Nick Irwin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.3cmgiu6

steps.title: Prepare O. marina cultures
steps.instruction: Feed O. marina (strain CCMP604) with heat‑killed E. coli, grow in f/2 medium on a 16 h light / 8 h dark cycle at 20 °C until the culture reaches at least 20 000 cells · mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Harvest and pellet cells
steps.instruction: Collect cells by centrifugation and retain the pellet for electroporation.

steps.title: Prepare electroporation mixture
steps.instruction: Add FITC‑dextran (Sigma FD70S) to the Biorad Gene Pulser Electroporation buffer to a final concentration of 2 mg mL⁻¹, then resuspend the O. marina pellet in 100 µL of this buffer.

steps.title: Load cells into cuvette
steps.instruction: Transfer the 100 µL cell suspension to a 0.2 cm electroporation cuvette.

steps.title: Electroporate cells
steps.instruction: Electroporate with a Biorad Gene Pulser Xcell using a square‑wave pulse. Choose one of the following settings:

substeps.instruction: 100 V, 3 × 5 ms pulses, 0.1 ms pause (standard condition).
75 V, 5 × 5 ms pulses, 0.1 ms pause (lower‑voltage alternative).

steps.title: Add recovery medium
steps.instruction: Immediately after the pulse, add 1 mL f/2 medium to the cuvette and transfer the entire volume to a microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Spin down and wash cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube for 3 min at 7 000 × g, discard the supernatant, and wash the pellet once with 1 mL f/2 medium.

steps.title: Recover cells in plates
steps.instruction: Resuspend the washed cells in fresh f/2 medium, dispense into a 24‑well plate, and incubate for 24 h before observation. For FITC‑dextran, keep the plate in the dark to avoid photobleaching.

steps.title: Count and prepare final samples
steps.instruction: Perform cell counts, then aliquot 1 000 000 cells per sample into a 50 mL Falcon tube and spin at 3 000 × g for 10 min.
